findings.claim: A shared UI field should be implemented in the owned @repo/ui/components/native and @repo/ui/components/web surfaces with matching names and props; app-local hand-built reusable fields and legacy UI imports are disallowed.

The field should remain a presentation component. API contracts and clients belong in @repo/core, while domain capability ownership, procedure declaration and routing belong in the Sanctuary API module/catalog and its subdomain card. The API surface is oRPC v2 under /api/v1; new clients must not add direct Supabase database, RPC, or realtime paths or import frozen @repo/core/api/*.

The older workflow's tRPC, Zustand-as-source-of-truth, and shared logic in packages/ui/packages/core prescriptions conflict with the current API and package boundaries and should not guide implementation without revision.

The older workflow's fixed palette, shadow, animation, blur and 2GB constraints conflict with current world-recipe styling and the platform's platform-specific UI kit rules; reconsider those prescriptions before applying them to this field.

The older workflow requires user approval of a plan before implementation, while the current supplied platform rules prescribe explore, align, implement and verify and state no such blanket plan-approval gate. This process conflict needs an explicit policy owner decision before implementation proceeds.
The specific capability, domain/subdomain, request/response contract, authorization policy, failure behavior, and field interaction requirements cannot be identified from these records alone.
